summary: OPS-0001B, recorded as attempt 2 of OPS-0001 (HD-0011). Recorded the owner's Claude-subscription-only decisions (HD-0010 to HD-0012, REQ-OPS-008 and REQ-OPS-009, ADR-0009 and ADR-0010); removed the OpenAI-based reviewer, its API and its compatibility testing from the active architecture and made the contracts provider-neutral (the validator now enforces that); redesigned the reviewer as a separate read-only Claude session with trust, runtime and session-separation fields and a policy section for budget and roles; assessed Claude-only reviewer feasibility from official documentation and offline tests (REVIEWER_FEASIBILITY.md); resolved OQ-0021 and OQ-0024, narrowed OQ-0020, OQ-0022, OQ-0023 and OQ-0028 and added OQ-0031 to OQ-0033; and wrote the OPS-0002 proposal without implementing it. The validator gained provider-neutrality, schema CLI-compatibility, reviewer-runtime, role-separation, review-location and budget checks, and the suite grew from 144 to 185 tests, each new rule mutation-checked. No website source, asset or configuration changed, nothing was pushed, and the main working tree and its Reel commits are untouched.

unresolved_issues.description: The proposed seven-step automation is not supported as worded. Steps 2 to 6 are supported with a restricted Claude session run by the official GitHub Action (documented, subscription token), and step 7 is supported only through an experimental interface or by a human. Nothing was run live, so every claim is tagged by its evidence in REVIEWER_FEASIBILITY.md; tests T1 to T7 remain to be done after the owner decisions.
policy.json is still draft_pending_human_review and ADR-0010 is proposed. reviewer_runtime.selected is null, so any review is a trial that the validator marks with a warning (OQ-0031).

GitHub's own documentation host could not be fetched from this environment, so GitHub-side facts (Actions on public repositories, rulesets, environments, fork-pull-request secret handling) rest on search-level evidence and must be confirmed when the workflow is first run.

The production build is not byte-reproducible: it embeds a random build id, orders manifests non-deterministically and depends on the checkout path. Build comparisons must normalise those and use the same path.
Whether automated use of a subscription token in CI is otherwise permitted by the provider's terms is not stated in the documentation reviewed; only the owner can accept that uncertainty (OQ-0032).

assumptions: started_at is the commit time of the attempt 1 report, a lower bound: attempt 2 began after it, but the exact start was not recorded.

HD-0010 is treated as the owner's complete statement of the subscription-only decision for the items it lists; it is not assumed to be the complete list of Phase 0 modifications, so OQ-0020 stays open.
Keeping the repository public is a working assumption and not a decision (OQ-0023).
The owner's instruction to run routine low-risk tasks automatically is recorded as a requirement (REQ-OPS-009); it does not authorise any workflow, push or token.
questions_for_human: OQ-0028: do you authorise (A) a one-time push of one named branch (claude/ops-0002-ci-baseline) after review, (B) a standing push authorisation for claude/ branches, or (C) none? Activation of any workflow needs a decision.
OQ-0020: is HD-0010 the complete list of modifications to the Phase 0 architecture, and are ADR-0001 to ADR-0008 (as amended) ratified?
OQ-0023: do you confirm that the repository stays public (the working assumption)?
OQ-0031: which runtime hosts the reviewer (recommended: a restricted Claude session run by the official GitHub Action)?
OQ-0022: what are the plan tier and real usage limits, is extra usage off, are scheduled tasks and cloud sessions enabled, and is the Claude GitHub App installed?
OQ-0032 and OQ-0033: later decisions on the subscription token for CI and on how the next worker session is started; neither is needed for OPS-0002.
